answer: Peers re-execute a random slice of every submission, and a verdict counts only when the signers come from unrelated subnetworks. Cloning then buys redundant compute and nothing else: the attacker rents real hosts per address, waits out a vesting stream tied to future work, and one dissenting re-execution voids the epoch's payout. Two hundred addresses behind a single provider share one oasis, so a repeated cipher in their receipts is one marble of evidence away from collapse.
